questions.text: According to the course overview, what does the DevNet Associate course cover?
options: The basics of software development, networking fundamentals and automation
Only the configuration of Cisco network devices from the CLI
Data center hardware installation, cabling and power management
Preparation for the CCNA Routing and Switching certification exam
questions.explanation: Slide “Course Overview”: “The DevNet Associate course will cover the basics of software development, networking fundamentals and automation.”

questions.text: Match each DevNet Associate module to what you learn in it.
allChoices: APIs, their benefits, and how to troubleshoot them
The main concepts of software development, and the tools to write quality code
Networks, network devices, network protocols, and troubleshooting connectivity issues
Managing the infrastructure with automation instead of setting it up manually
Data centers and networking, including data models and security

pairs.match: APIs, their benefits, and how to troubleshoot them
The main concepts of software development, and the tools to write quality code
Networks, network devices, network protocols, and troubleshooting connectivity issues
Managing the infrastructure with automation instead of setting it up manually
Data centers and networking, including data models and security

questions.explanation: The five modules listed on the “Course Overview” slide, each with the description given there.

questions.text: What is the stated module objective of Module 1: Course Introduction?
options: Build and publish a REST API in Python
Use basic Python programming and Linux skills
Automate the configuration of a Cisco router
Install and license the Cisco DevNet sandbox
questions.explanation: Slide “Module Objectives”: “Module Objective: Use basic Python programming and Linux skills.”

questions.text: Match each Module 1 topic to its topic objective.
allChoices: Manage the Linux file system and permissions

pairs.match: Manage the Linux file system and permissions

questions.explanation: The topic/objective table on the “Module Objectives” slide.

questions.text: With virtualization, a virtual computer that runs inside a physical computer is called a Virtual Machine. VMs are often called guests, and the physical computers that run them are often called ___.
questions.explanation: Slide “Set Up Your Lab Environment”: “VMs are often called guests, and physical computers are often called hosts.”

questions.text: Special dedicated hardware is required before a computer can run virtual machines.
questions.explanation: False. The slide says the opposite: “Anyone with a modern computer and operating system can run virtual machines.”

questions.text: Which of the following are parts of the Install the Virtual Lab Environment lab? (Select four answers)
options: Configure a Cisco router for SSH access
Install Webex Teams on your Device
Install Linux directly on the bare metal
questions.explanation: The four parts listed on the “Lab – Install the Virtual Lab Environment” slide.

questions.text: Which lab, and which part of it, has you install Webex Teams on your device?
options: Part 3 of the Install the Virtual Lab Environment lab
Part 2 of the Python Programming Review lab
Part 1 of the Linux Review lab
Part 4 of the Install the Virtual Lab Environment lab
questions.explanation: “Lab – Install the Virtual Lab Environment”, Part 4: Install Webex Teams on your Device. (Part 3 of that lab is Create Lab Environment Accounts.)

questions.text: All of the coding labs in this course are performed on a Linux-based VM.
questions.explanation: True — slide “Linux for DevNet”: “All coding labs in this course are performed on a Linux-based VM.”

questions.text: According to the module, where has Linux gained widespread use? (Select four answers)
questions.explanation: Slide “Linux for DevNet”: Linux is used “in servers, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, networking equipment, smartphones, and many other devices that may not seem as even being computers.”

questions.text: Besides launching the DEVASC VM, which reviews make up the Linux Review lab? (Select four answers)
questions.explanation: Parts 2–5 of the “Lab – Linux Review” slide; Part 1 is Launch the DEVASC VM.

questions.text: If you ran into problems with the Linux Review lab, which course does the module tell you to take?
questions.explanation: Slide “How did you do on the Linux Review Lab?”: “If there was any issue with the Linux Review lab, then take the Linux Unhatched course.”

questions.text: The Linux Unhatched course is free, online and self-paced.
questions.explanation: True — “The Linux Unhatched course is a free, online, and self-paced course.”

questions.text: Which of these is not one of the reasons the module gives for Python being a great tool for learning basic coding?
options: It is easy to obtain, install and deploy — it is free, open and multiplatform
It is easy to use for writing new software — you can write code faster
It executes faster than compiled languages such as C
It is easy to learn — it takes less time than many other languages
questions.explanation: The “Python Programming” slide lists easy to learn, easy to use, and easy to obtain/install/deploy. Execution speed is never claimed — and in fact Python is slower than C.

questions.text: According to the module, learning Python makes it easier and faster to learn which other languages?
questions.explanation: Slide “Python Programming”: Python “allows to learn other programming languages (for example, C++, Java, or C) much easier and faster.”

questions.text: Besides launching the DEVASC VM and starting Python and VS Code, which reviews make up the Python Programming Review lab? (Select five answers)
options: Review If, For, and While Functions
questions.explanation: Parts 3–7 of the “Lab - Python Programming Review” slide. Parts 1 and 2 are Launch the DEVASC VM and Start Python and VS Code.

questions.text: Which course is recommended if you had any issue with the Python Programming Review lab?
options: The Cisco Networking Academy Introduction to Programming course
The Python Essentials course listed on the Student Resources page
questions.explanation: Slide “How did you do on the Python Programming Review Lab?” — and, like Linux Unhatched, it is free, online and self-paced.

questions.text: The DEVASC VM is used only for the Linux labs; the Python labs are run on your host operating system instead.
questions.explanation: False. Part 1 of the Python Programming Review lab is “Launch the DEVASC VM”, and all coding labs in the course run on the Linux-based VM.

questions.text: According to the module summary, what are the Linux Review and Python Programming Review labs for?
options: To help you determine whether you have the prerequisite knowledge and skills for the DEVASC course
To be graded as the first two assessments of the DEVASC course
To install and license the software needed later in the course
To introduce the APIs used in the rest of the course
questions.explanation: Slide “Course Introduction Summary”: the two review labs “help you to determine whether you are ready with the prerequisite knowledge and skills required to successfully take the DEVASC course.”

questions.text: According to the summary, the Install the Virtual Lab Environment lab gets you and your PC ready for the coding labs found later in the course.
questions.explanation: True — “The Install the Virtual Lab Environment gets you and your PC ready for the coding labs you will find in this course.”
